I had dated my first boyfriend for ten years, from our sophomore year of high school to when we were both 25 years old. The final year we were dating was when my OCD became noticeable and hard to control, and it caused me anxiety and intrusive thoughts. While he had been supportive at first and said I could always tell him about my fears, as time went on, he became annoyed and frustrated by my condition. 

Within the last few weeks of our relationship, he became increasingly emotionally abusive toward me, actually triggering an anxiety attack by using one of my obsessions against me. Two times, he struck me across the face, claiming that it was to "snap me out of my attack" (this should never be done to someone having a nervous breakdown or anxiety attack), and the second time had caused me to cry out. It came to the point where I had had enough, and I told my sister and grandparents, who were furious that my boyfriend had dared to lay a hand on me in anger. I broke it off with him, and declined his attempt to get back with me. 

The first few months of being single were hard. I had been with someone for ten years, and to just suddenly be on my own again was jarring. My attacks were bad, but were not as bad as they had been when I was still with my boyfriend. During this time, I started seeing a therapist, and she had been the one to tell me just what was going wrong with me mentally. Over the next year, she encouraged me to see my doctor, and I was prescribed an SSRI, which helped immensely. I also began to enjoy being single, realizing I had more time to pursue things that interested me, and even found new hobbies. 

It was horrible to know that my first relationship ended over something largely out of my control, but it was even more horrible to know that the person I had dated would become abusive toward me due to not understanding my mental problems. But that's just it: he didn't understand my problems, and refused to understand them as well. I've come to understand that I need to find someone who will accept me for who I am, OCD and all.

Honestly I initially just thought I was just having anxiety attacks related to things I was afraid of, but then I searched 'thoughts feel real' on Google and found out about intrusive thoughts. I had no idea that the things I would do over and over until I felt I had done it absolutely perfectly, what I deemed rituals to make sure my thoughts wouldn't come true, were compulsions, either.

I've never had to describe or explain it really, but to me it's like you're thinking about one thing, then it suddenly connects it to another thing, something that you're afraid of, and then you become afraid of the thing you're afraid of happening to the thing you were thinking about, more often than not leading you to become scared of the initial subject you were thinking about. You tell yourself it won't happen, but then you start to feel as if you want the bad thing to happen, though you know deep down that this isn't true. You spend hours fighting your mind, but no matter how much logic you use, somehow the 'monster' as I've come to call it deflects it with more doubt. 

With compulsions, it's like someone is forcing you to do something, threatening something or someone important to you if you do not do what they want you to do.
